items.title: Why Is Eaton Priced Above Peers That Earn More Per Sale?
items.summary: Eaton (ETN) grew revenue 15.5% over the past twelve months, faster than any of the five industrial peers it is measured against. It trades at 41.5 times earnings, against roughly 32 times for the next two names in the group. At $409.15 a share as of September 10, 2026, what that premium buys is an operating margin that ranks fourth of six.

items.title: What Happens To CAT Stock If Data Center Demand Cools?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) stock returned 94% over the past twelve months, against 17.9% for the S&P 500, and its second quarter of 2026 was the first in company history above $20 billion of sales and revenues. One risk to that run is a quiet one. Caterpillar is adding factory capacity with data center power as a big driver, and analysts are asking whether that demand has staying power through 2030.

items.title: Is Eaton Stock Amplifying A Risk You Already Own?
items.summary: Eaton (ETN) makes the power equipment that goes inside data centers, among much else, and it has climbed 5.0% over the last five trading days while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%. A run like that pulls money in. The question worth answering is not where the stock goes from here. It is what owning Eaton does to the rest of your money every time the market moves, and it moves further than the index in both directions.

items.title: Cummins Sells the Power Solutions That Keep Data Centers Running. Does That Make the Stock a Buy?
items.summary: Its shares have surged so far in 2026, and there could still be plenty of upside ahead.

items.title: CAT Could Be the Best AI Infrastructure Stock You’re Overlooking
items.summary: While everyone fixates on chips and software, one 100-year-old manufacturer is quietly racking up orders that stretch to 2030 and posting the biggest quarter in its history, powered by the same AI buildout driving Nvidia headlines.

items.title: Is Cummins Stock Outperforming the Nasdaq?
items.summary: Cummins has outpaced the Nasdaq Composite over the past year, and analysts remain moderately bullish about the stock’s outlook.

items.title: Can Data Center Power Fuel CAT Stock To New Highs?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) has almost doubled over the past year, gaining 96.3% while the S&P 500 returned 19.1%. Deere and Cummins each gained about 43%. The broader machinery cycle carried Caterpillar part of the way, but enthusiasm around power generation drove the premium. The gap to the stock's 52-week high is what a buyer now has to price against those expectations.
